title: A minimal rule for a feature hints that a system was made for a purpose

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A minimal rule for a feature hints that a system was made for a purpose

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since purposes can always be reinterpreted as mechanisms, purpose cannot be identified for certain from behavior; the best criterion is that a system is the minimal or optimal one producing a given feature, which suggests it was built for that purpose, as advanced technology should increasingly use minimal systems.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: finding out that the rule for the system is the minimal or optimal one for producing that feature may make it seem more likely that at least with sufficiently advanced technology the system might have specifically been created for the purpose of exhibiting that feature.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Intelligence in the Universe” (from p. 822), p. 834. Scope: recognizing purpose in artifacts and signals, including extraterrestrial ones

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-49: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.29

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A restricted statistical association between known design and approximate minimality could be tested after compiling a corpus. No existing public resource directly supplies certified minimal rules and provenance across the intended scope, and minimality cannot uniquely identify purpose.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a corpus with known provenance, estimate whether systems are minimal for selected features and compare minimality distributions between designed and natural systems. Likelihood ratios could test minimality as evidence of purpose, but not establish purpose with certainty or extrapolate to advanced extraterrestrial technology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Global minimality is generally uncomputable or search-space dependent.

Natural selection can also produce optimization.

Known artifact corpora poorly represent advanced technology.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data existence: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.28
data adequacy: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Minimality is a computable property once a feature is formalized. The sentence uses it as a sign of purpose, while also saying that purposes can be rewritten as mechanisms and that a purposeless search can discover minimal rules. Those concessions leave no outcome that favors creation-for-a-purpose over a rival that denies purpose.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Given a feature, test whether the observed rule is minimal among rules that produce it, and treat minimality as evidence of purpose. The text notes that an unguided exhaustive search can find the same minimum, so the observation fits design and blind search alike.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim says purpose can be redescribed as mechanism, so behavior never identifies purpose with certainty.

Seem more likely is a degree of suspicion rather than a decision threshold.

A minimal rule can be the output of a purposeless search.
